item.description:

item.title: Gemini Notebook: your AI research assistant — Wed Nov 18, 10:00 AM — Online
item.description:
Discover how source-grounded AI differs from LLMs like, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini In this brief introduction to Gemini Notebook, you’ll learn how to upload a variety of sources, analyze dense scholarly articles, and chat directly with your personal research. It uses your exact source citations, thus reducing those troublesome AI hallucinations. We'll also explore the Studio to turn your Notebook into: study tools, detailed reports, beautiful slide presentations, infographics and videos. Gemini Notebook can also aggregate, cross reference, extract data and identify key findings from your uploaded sources. Register Here: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/18024894
Hosted by: Sprague Library
Online Location: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/18024894
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12982239

item.title: Rethinking Thanksgiving Through Food Sovereignty — Wed Nov 18, 11:45 AM — Schmitt Hall
item.description:
Join the New Jersey Center for Indigenous Justice for a discussion on our relationship to food, farming, and each other. Learn about how Indigenous knowledge and food sovereignty principles strengthen our connection to this land, mitigate harm throughout our food systems, and bring people together in community. Led by Ares Cabigting (Program Coordinator for Native Roots Farm Foundation) and Joy Youwakim (Founder of Saboon Maazeh) this will be the final installment in the NJCIJ's Native American Heritage Month Lecture series. All are welcome! Questions? Contact covanrodrigk1@montclair.edu
Hosted by:

item.title: The Party Scene - FREE Tickets for Students — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — Kasser Theater
item.description:
The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham: The Party Scene
Sun., November 22 @ 3PM
Exquisitely eclectic quartet The Hands Free and members of the fabulously whimsical Dance Heginbotham join forces in The Party Scene. Inspired by The Nutcracker and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters. About The Hands Free: The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers James Moore (guitar & banjo), Caroline Shaw (violin), Nathan Koci (accordion), and Eleonore Oppenheim (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures and explosive improvisations. item.title: Book Talk: 20 Over 60 by Beth Weinhouse and David Galef — Thu Dec 3, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
In their new anthology 20 OVER 60 (Regal House; October 6, 2026), editors Beth Weinhouse and David Galef—also co-editors of the anthology 20 OVER 40—present a portrait of later life that is consistently overlooked, in a culture obsessed with youth. The twenty short stories—including ones by Joyce Carol Oates, Paul Theroux, and Jane Gardam—are vibrant, moving, and often hilarious, capturing the texture of life after sixty in all its complexity.
Among the characters readers will meet: a retired couple whose hobby is stealing pepper mills from high-end restaurants, a woman juggling her husband and ex-husband staying in the same hospital, a futuristic nursing home whose designers become its unhappy residents, an older woman trying her hand at online dating, and a grandfather helping his granddaughter scatter her mother's ashes. These smart and poignant stories make the case that the years after sixty are as strange, surprising, and vivid as the decades that came before—and that readers li

item.title: Clean slate;NOVA Fashion Show — Fri Dec 4, 6:00 PM — University Hall 7500 - Conference Center
item.description:
Clean Slate is a fashion show centered around new beginnings, reinvention, and the freedom to redefine yourself. Through fashion, movement, and creative expression, NOVA invites students to explore what it means to leave behind what no longer serves them and step into something new. Each look represents a different interpretation from shedding old identities and expectations to embracing growth, individuality, and transformation. Clean Slate is not about erasing the past, it’s about recognizing that you have the freedom to create what comes next. Come experience a night where fashion becomes a blank canvas and every person gets the chance to tell a new story.
Hosted by: New Generation Of Visionary Artists
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12984522
Source: Montclair State University

item.title: Chloe Flower — Sun Feb 14, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Run Time: 1 hour 30 mins, no intermission
Pianist, composer, and multi-hyphenate star Chloe Flower brings her signature “popsical” approach to bridging pop and classical music to an immersive interdisciplinary experience featuring her original works, dance, and cinematic video. Blending classical elegance with contemporary energy, Chloe redefines the modern piano performance through her boundary-pushing artistry, captivating audiences worldwide. An official Steinway Artist, Chloe creates a powerful fusion of music, movement, and visual storytelling. Featuring students from the John J. Cali School of Music at Montclair State University and Kaufman Music Center’s Special Music School. Presented in collaboration with the John J. Cali School of Music.
Source: PEAK Performances at MSU

item.title: Dungeons and Dragons One Shot: Turkey Trouble — Fri Nov 20, 7:00 PM — The Player Agency
item.description:
Adventurers! Join us for a fun and fantastical one shot D&D campaign. We embrace the quirky, the chaotic, and the downright silly. No experience necessary, we welcome players of all skill levels. We’re all about having a good laugh and creating unforgettable memories together. Players aged 16 and up are welcome to play. This is a safe space for all, including LGBTQIA+ and Neurodiverse folk. Players will be playing the one shot: Turkey Trouble: In the quiet village of Gibbingtowne, renowned for its annual Fall Festival, something strange has befallen the villagers: they’ve all been transformed into turkeys! As the adventurers investigate the source of this peculiar curse, they must contend with the looming threat of being transformed into turkeys themselves while racing to uncover the truth behind the magical mishap. item.title: An Evening with Dark Star Orchestra — Fri Nov 20, 8:00 PM — The Wellmont Theater
item.description:
Performing to critical acclaim for nearly 30 years and over 3300 shows, Dark Star Orchestra continues the Grateful Dead live concert experience. The seven-piece band performs shows based on actual Grateful Dead set lists from their 30 years of touring, or creates unique sets from the Dead’s extensive catalog. This approach allows fans both young and old to share in the experience while offering a continually evolving artistic outlet within this musical canon. item.title: Tired of Doing All The Heavy Lifting in Your Relationships? — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — The Space
item.description: Are you the one who always remembers, plans, initiates conversations, keeps the peace, and makes sure everyone else is okay? Whether it’s your marriage, partnership, family, friendships, or other relationships, carrying the emotional weight can leave you feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, and disconnected. Join Sakirat Oladiran, Nurse Practitioner and Certified Life & Health Coach, for an intimate and supportive wellness gathering designed for women. We’ll explore how relationship stress impacts your physical and emotional health, why you may find yourself carrying more than your share, and practical ways to communicate your needs, establish healthy boundaries, and create more balanced, fulfilling connections. This is an opportunity to pause, reflect, feel heard, and walk away with practical strategies to support both your relationships and your well-being. Come as you are. Leave with a fresh perspective and tools to create healthier connections. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens

item.title: Three Stories. One Screen. | The Official Film Showcase — Sat Nov 21, 1:30 PM — The Clairidge
item.description: Dive into three stories on one screen at The Official Film Showcase—live and in person at The Clairidge in Montclair, NJ! Headlining the afternoon is End of the Line: Brotherhood, a raw, poignant feature drama examining end-of-life dignity, caregiver burnout, and the historical roots of healthcare distrust in the Black community through the lens of an underfunded inner-city hospice clinic. Shot using 6K digital cinema technology, the film features an ensemble cast including veteran actors Christopher Mann (The Wire, Creed III) and Nakia Dillard (The Wire, Black Lightning). The program also showcases the exclusive premiere of short drama Wedding Night and psychological thriller Lady in the Mirror. Guests will enjoy light food, networking opportunities, and an interactive post-screening filmmaker talkback with cast and crew from all films discussing the story, production journey, and social impact behind the work. Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Time: 1:30 PM – 5:00 PM EST Venue: The
